docs/how-it-works.md:19:2. **Check the author** ([`src/security.ts`](../src/security.ts)). See [Security](security.md#who-can-start-pi). If the author cannot start pi, the run stops and writes a warning to the log.
docs/how-it-works.md:26:9. **Save.** pi-action pushes the thread. Then it writes the git commands that read the thread to the log and the job summary. See [Read a thread](threads.md#read-a-thread).
docs/extensions.md:57:pi-action ignores these parts of a pi extension and writes a warning to the log:
docs/extensions.md:82:- If a package has `pi.durable` and `pi.extensions`, pi-action loads only the `pi.durable` entry, because its pi extensions need the pi coding agent. pi-action writes this to the log.
docs/extensions.md:137:- **Notifications.** `ui.notify` writes to the log and to the job summary, not to comments.
docs/threads.md:27:To save threads, the job needs `contents: write`. Without it, the run works but cannot save the thread, and pi-action writes a warning to the log.
docs/threads.md:41:- If two runs on one thread push at the same time, the remote rejects the later push. pi-action writes this to the log and does not overwrite the history of the other run. The run that was rejected stops pushing.
docs/threads.md:42:- pi-action retries other push failures (a network error, or `[remote rejected] ... (failed)` from GitHub) after 1, 3, and 10 seconds. If all retries fail, pi-action writes a warning to the log, and the next push tries again.
docs/threads.md:45:- **The `Save pi thread state` step leaves a remote that is ahead alone.** If the remote already has the local commits, for example because the main step pushed them, the step writes `already saved` to the log, not a warning.
docs/threads.md:111:- With a token without `contents: write`, pi-action cannot push the refs. It writes a warning to the log, as for threads.
docs/threads.md:127:The workflow log of each run on a thread shows these commands for that thread, in the group `How to read refs/pi/threads/<number> with git`, after the last push of the run. The job summary of the run shows them too. Each answer comment of pi-action shows the ref of its thread, and the `git fetch` command.
README.md:9:- **One conversation per issue or pull request.** A later `@pi` comment continues the thread. pi keeps everything it saw and did before, also the files it left uncommitted. The workflow log shows the git commands that [read the thread](docs/threads.md#read-a-thread). See [Durable threads](docs/threads.md).
